newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CLOSES FIRMER AGAINST HARD UNITS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CLOSES FIRMER AGAINST HARD UNITS.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar closed on Tuesday firmer against most hard units on the back of a wave of foreign currency off-loading by a number of banks, dealers said.
"There's been a flood of foreign currency in the market from Friday. People are just selling, selling, selling," one dealer said.
He said it appeared that some speculators in the market could have been hoarding foreign currency which they now had no use for.
"But no one is really sure where the money is coming from," the dealer added.

At the end of Tuesday trade, the Zimbabwe dollar was quoted on the interbank market at 11.1225/1325 against the U.S. dollar, up from Monday's 11.1450/1550 and was also stronger versus sterling at 17.9730/18.0000 compared to 18.2000/2200.
It edged up to 6.5075/5150 from 6.5900/6000 against the mark but finished easier on the rand at 2.4995/5035 from 2.4950/5050
